Decision on the clause: 3.6.4.1.2 says the interval grows with the
distance travelled by the odometer's accuracy; the gamma terms of
3.6.4.1.5 follow the Train Data and the Supervised Manoeuvre state. The
Tick post's clause holds for the odometer's part, the gamma terms
excluded, and its expression is unchanged: `EVC_Position.Doubt_Over` /
`Doubt_Under` are that part now (Q_LOCACC and the over- and
under-reading amounts), `Gamma_Over` / `Gamma_Under` the terms in force
and `Interval_Over` / `Interval_Under` the whole interval (used by
`Min_Safe_Front`, `Max_Safe_Front`, the SOLR ones, the kept position's
Q_LOCACC and the position reports). B1400's proposal (the gamma terms
unchanged as a fourth condition of the antecedent) does not prove
without a frame "the gamma terms unchanged" in the post of every step
before `Sync_Train_Length`, across five units; the split needs none
(every step's `Doubt_Over = Doubt_Over'Old` holds as before).

One term, never two: `Gamma_Over` is `Manoeuvre.Over` from the first
authorisation (`Shift_For_Manoeuvre`) to `End_Manoeuvre`, else the new
state set by `EVC_Position.Set_Gamma` (the consist's terms in front of
the engine when the orientation is the active cab's or no cab is
active, in rear of it when opposite, by `Consist_End`).
`EVC_Core.Modes.Sync_Train_Length` sets it once a cycle: SB without
valid Train Data with the safe consist length available, or a request
pending (`EVC_Sessions.SM_Waiting`; decision: the safe consist length
last received), never with the manoeuvre's orientation. The report of
131 (`Consist_Report`, A045) takes the consist's terms in place of
those in force (`Fill` and `Report_With` take terms, not a widening).

`Scenario_SM_Gamma`; `Scenario_SM_Authorisation`'s same direction check
measures from the odometer's part. Outside the named units:
`test/src/s076_bench.adb` (`Doubt_Over` / `Doubt_Under` read the whole
interval). SUBSET-076: 1084 / 1098 / 1008 before and after, 0
regressions, 0 improvements; no golden changed.

bit 0 ready (SH, 4.4.8.1.4; SM, 4.4.21.1.13), bit 1 in SM the engine
orientation opposite to the direction of the MA
(`EVC_Position.Manoeuvre_Direction` 2), sent when it changes by
`EVC_Core.Outputs.Send_Remote_Shunting` (state `TIU_RS_Sent` in the
parent's private part). Decision: an output of its own rather than a
fourth byte of the commands: their length of 3 is what the hosts
(`Sim_Onboard_Env`) and the test helpers key on, and every recorded
brake command would change the goldens; a host that does not know the
tag ignores the record. Decision: the mode is the condition (the
clauses name none other). `Scenario_SM_Remote_Shunting` decodes the
frame (SM same and opposite, out of SM, SH). B015's part closed. No
golden changed; SUBSET-076 1084 / 1098 / 1008, 0 regressions.

### The DMI protocol's rest: the DMI's report of the message ends it owns, the Train Data and network ID for the data view (e6/protocol-rest) (2026-10-24)

- B1700: MSG_STATUS_ENDED 16#42# (DMI to EVC, entry u8), one frame per
  system status message the DMI ends by itself (its 30 s timers from the
  start or from event 2, a mode change of DMI 15.1.1.2, a button of the
  Main window); not for the ends the on-board knows (its event 1, with
  the 30 s after it, and the acknowledgement). Decision: one message per
  end carrying the catalogue entry, since `EVC_JRU_Records.System_Status`
  clears one bit per entry; the DMI's whole set would race with the
  starts the on-board sent in the same cycle. `DMI_System_Status.Take_Ended`,
  `DMI_Core.Report_Status_Ends`; `EVC_DMI_Port.Valid_Input_Frame` accepts
  it, `EVC_Driver_Requests` latches up to 16 per cycle (`Status_End`),
  `EVC_Core.Records.Record_System_Status` applies them (three lines, an
  edit outside the package's units) and the existing change detection
  writes the message 23. The bench page routes the frame; the fuzzer
  sends it. Runner unchanged (no step judges a DMI-owned end).
- B1760: MSG_STORED_VALUES grows to 64 bytes: after the 34 of the short
  form, train_valid u8, the 12 bytes of MSG_DRIVER_DATA kind 2 in the
  on-board's codes (L_TRAIN m, %, V_MAXTRAIN km/h, NC_CDTRAIN, NC_TRAIN,
  M_AXLELOADCAT, M_AIRTIGHT, M_LOADINGGAUGE), network_len u8 and 16 bytes
  (the digits of NID_MN as MSG_RADIO_NETWORKS names it, only when the
  network is known). The DMI reads both lengths; `DMI_Train_Data.Take_Onboard`
  maps the codes back to the positions of Tables 41 and 42;
  `DMI_Data_View.Value_Of` shows the on-board's Train Data and network
  once a long form came, the DMI's entries before (no DMI golden
  changed). `EVC_Core.Outputs.Send_Stored_Values` sends the frame when
  it differs from the last one sent (`EVC_Core.Values_Sent` replaces
  `ID_Sent` and `TRN_Sent`). Fifteen on-board goldens: the frame 30
  bytes longer, a frame added at each change of the Train Data; in
  valid_inputs a JRU record taken one Take later (the 2048-byte take
  buffer of the test full).
- Left: the row 3.18.6.1 re-read against the clause (not taken, the
  bound reached), partial.

  4.4.15.1.5, 4.4.20.1.10 ask, "if possible", that a safety critical
  fault in SL, NL or PS does not stop the train: memorised, handled when
  the mode is left, and (SL, NL) an error to the RBC, packet 4 M_ERROR 6
  in the next message 136 (7.5.1.64; to an RBC of system version 1 the
  value 7, 6.6.3.4.5). The sequences: 3160400_02 steps 53 to 56 (NL,
  level 2: the fault, the JRU 27, the 136 with packet 4 M_ERROR 6, the
  JRU 10, then power off), 6060303_01 steps 220 to 223 (the same with
  the RBC in version 1); today 3160400_02 is blocked at step 17 and
  6060303_01 fails at step 81, both before. `EVC_Core.Enter_Failure` is
  the host's call after a failed operation: the on-board's state is not
  to be trusted then, so it stays the fail-silent entry. What a fault
  the on-board can live with needs: (a) a second entry point,
  `EVC_Core.Report_Fault (Kind)`, called by the host for a fault it
  detected outside the on-board's computation (a self-test, a redundant
  channel's disagreement, a monitored peripheral), never from an
  exception handler; in SL, NL and PS it sets a memorised fault in
  `EVC_Core` state, writes the JRU 27 at once (`EVC_Core.Records.Record_Fault`)
  and asks `EVC_Sessions.Reports.Request_Error` for M_ERROR 6 on the
  supervising session when one is established (SL, NL; not PS, whose
  clause has no report); in any other mode it is `Enter_Failure`;
  (b) at the next mode change out of SL, NL or PS, `EVC_Core.Modes`
  applies the memorised fault as condition [13] (SF) before the new mode
  is taken, so the train is stopped only once it is a leading engine
  again; (c) the proof shape: a postcondition that a reported fault in
  SL, NL, PS leaves the mode unchanged and Failed False with the fault
  memorised, and an invariant of the mode machine that no mode other
  than SL, NL, PS, SF and NP is reached with a fault memorised;
  (d) the bench and the runner: `S076_Run`'s "SIM fault safety-critical"
  calls the new entry, not `Enter_Failure`. Open decision for the
  coordinator: whether the hosts (hosted, wasm, TMS570) have any fault
  of kind (a) to report; without one the entry point is test-only, and
  the clauses' "if possible" is met by the fail-silent decision of
  B1720.

Lambda only, `EVC_Mission.Train_Data_Of` gave empty curves, the
snapshot's `Extra.Train` was the defaults (`Build_Train`).

**The image, format version 2** (`EVC_Config`, layout in
`evc_config.ads`): bytes 0 to 31 as version 1 (version 2, the length
L); 32 the braking model (0 lambda, 1 gamma); 33 the special brakes the
vehicle has (bits regenerative, eddy current, magnetic shoe, Ep); a
lambda train ends there (CRC at 34, L = 38). A gamma train continues
field after field: the reaction and equivalent build up times of the
emergency and the service brake (u16 ms, 0 to 60 s), A_brake_emergency
(1 to 8 steps), A_brake_service (1 to 8), A_brake_normal_service (0 to
8), Kdry_rst for M_NVEBCL 0 to 9 and Kwet_rst (8 u16 thousandths each,
one per step of A_brake_emergency, 0 to 2.000), Kn+ and Kn- (0 to 8),
M_rotating_nom (0 to 100 %), a byte for the normal service sets (then
A_SB01, A_SB12 and the three models in G, then in P), a byte for the
models by combination (then 8 emergency and 8 service curves for the
combinations of regenerative, eddy current and magnetic shoe brake, 16
pairs of times for the emergency and 16 for the service brake by the
four brakes, Table 4), the CRC-32 at L - 4. A step function is a count
byte and (u16 speed cm/s, u16 deceleration mm/s²) pairs, the speeds
strictly rising. L runs from 38 to 1248 (`Max_Image_Length`, every
curve at 8 steps with the sets and the combinations). Decisions: the
version decides the length (version 1 stays 36 bytes and accepted); a
value or count out of range is `Bad_Field`, fields that end before or
run past the CRC `Bad_Length`; the gamma train is package state of
`EVC_Config` (`Gamma_T`), not a part of `Config_T`, because `Current`
returns `Config_T` by value at many places (2.5 KB more each); it is
read in place by `Gamma_Models (D)` and `Gamma_Extra (X)`.
`Encode_V2` writes the image (the bench's tool next round); the
decoder is `Get`, `Get_Curve`, `Get_Factors`, `Get_Normal_Service`,
`Get_Combinations`, `Get_Gamma` under `Decoded` (`Get_Train`), the
gamma state is filled at `Load` (`Load_Gamma`).

**The Train Data of a Gamma train**: `EVC_Mission.Train_Data_Of` takes
the installation's models when `Fixed_Train_T.Model` is Gamma; the
snapshot's `Extra.Train` is the installation's
(`EVC_Stored_Information.Build_Train`, `EVC_Config.State` added to its
Global, its caller `Build` had it). Decision: the brake percentage a
gamma train's driver enters (the DMI's Train Data window has the field
whatever the model, DMI 11.3.9.9.1) is checked and kept for the data
view and the JRU; no model is derived from it (3.13.2.2.5.1;
`EVC_Braking.Conversion_Applicable` is Lambda only).

### The stored radio information: the three sets of the transition buffer, the row applied to the packets of their own units, the Supervised Manoeuvre default train of a gamma installation (e6/radio-stored) (2026-10-25)

**The three sets (B1920 done).** Premise checked: the buffer
(`EVC_Radio_Authority.Buffer`) already kept three messages, the oldest
replaced, deleted by 4.8.5.4 a) to c) and released at the transition;
what it did not keep was a general message whose packets on the rows R
[2] of Table 4.8.3 the first filter stores (`Packet_Filter` Stored):
`EVC_Stored_Information.Take_Radio` took them at once. Now
`EVC_Radio_Authority.Keep_Level_2_Part` keeps such a message 24 as a set
(level 2 announced, or a level transition order in the message,
4.8.1.3.1 step 1), `Take_Radio` no longer takes a Stored packet, and at
the release (`Released_Part`, the slot's `EVC_Radio_Info.Slot_T.Level_2_Part`)
only the packets on the rows R [2] are taken. Decision: the message is
kept whole and the row applied again at the release (4.8.5.2.1: the set
is the part neither accepted nor rejected at once); its other packets
are taken at the reception. Decision: with an order in the message, step
2 of 4.8.1.3.1 is the buffer's own: released in the same cycle when the
order makes the level 2 (`Release_Transition_Buffer`), deleted at the
next `Buffer.Update` when it is for another level (4.8.5.4 a). The
special case of a message 24 with 51 or 52 kept whole and not taken
(e5/buffer-radio) is folded into it: its other packets are now taken at
once. `EVC_Radio_Info.Max_Messages` 2 -> 5: three released sets beside
the cycle's two (the third released message was refused before, also
for the messages 3 of `Scenario_Transition_Buffer`; 4.8 KB of static
storage). Scenario `EVC_Test_Authority.Scenario_Buffer_Three_Sets`
(adhesion, track condition, level crossing, then a PBD replacing the
adhesion; none used before the transition; the three taken at it, the
replaced one not; an order to level 0 by a balise group deletes a set).

### The fixed Train Data entry: the type of entry and the pre-configured train types on the protocol, the fixed and switchable layouts, the driver's train type as the Train Data (e6/fixed-entry) (2026-10-25)

- The type of entry: MSG_ONBOARD train bits 6 and 7 from TIU signal 16
  (`EVC_Core.Outputs.Train_Bits`, `EVC_DMI_Port.Train_Entry_*`): 0 not
  known (no input yet), 1 fixed, 2 flexible, 3 switchable. Decision,
  narrowing the brief (which had 0 fixed, 3 not known): 0 is "not known",
  read as flexible, so that an EVC that never sets the bits (EVC_Mock,
  the goldens' frames) keeps the flexible entry; no MSG_ONBOARD byte of
  any golden changed. `DMI_Conditions.Train_Entry`.
- MSG_TRAIN_TYPES 16#12# (EVC to DMI): count u8 (0 .. Train_Types_Max 8),
  per type name_len u8 (1 .. 16) and Latin-1 bytes, then the 12 bytes of
  MSG_DRIVER_DATA kind 2 (length u16 m, brake percentage u16, max speed
  u16 km/h, NC_CDTRAIN u8, NC_TRAIN u16, M_AXLELOADCAT u8, M_AIRTIGHT u8,
  M_LOADINGGAUGE u8; decision: the codes the DMI already maps, not the

  `dmi_fuzz` offers the message; `evc_fuzz` unchanged (an output only).

### Four bookkeeping items: the level 2 trip for a linked group at the EOA in release speed monitoring, the override ended by an MA of the RBC and by the SR list, the texts deleted by a shortening, a balise group read in SL, PS or SH against the orientation (e5/bookkeeping-4) (2026-10-25)

B842 (done): the line held at the source, C_11 was never set. The level 1
counterpart [12] is only the min safe antenna passing the EOA
(3.13.10.2.7), so there was no linking reading to reuse.
`EVC_Radio_Authority.Linked_Group_At_EOA` measures both locations from
the group the EOA's location is referred to (the anchor of its origin's
estimated item: the MA's reference, or the group it was relocated to).
The group's first possible location is its linking distance from that
group (none for the group itself) less its location accuracy. It holds
when this is beyond the EOA less the antenna to front end distance
(strictly: "in rear by a distance shorter than"). `Evaluate` holds C_11
with it in release speed monitoring (`Facts_T.Release_Monitoring`, from
`EVC_Core.Modes.Evaluate_Radio`), in level 2, while the override is not
active (5.8.3.6). `Evaluate` and `Evaluate_Radio` now read
`EVC_Origins.State`. A first reading that took the old LRBG's frame
position held the condition wrongly 11 m in rear: the relocation on the
group moves the origins.
Finding: in this position model the relocation on the linked group makes
its accuracy the confidence interval, so [16] (the min safe front end
past the EOA) holds in the same cycle whenever [11] does.
`Scenario_Linked_Group_At_EOA` checks the condition in the cycle of the
reading. Rows 3.13.10.2.6, b) and its three bullets are done, and the
note of the 4.6.3 Table row is updated.

override on `Context_T.Radio_MA_L2` (f), end 6: an MA of the RBC accepted
in the cycle in level 2) and on `Context_T.SR_Unlisted` (g), end 7, beside
the SH list: with the list of packet 63 stored, a group passed in the
cycle is not in it, `EVC_Radio_Authority.Group_Passed_Unlisted`). Both are
set by `EVC_Core.Modes`. [36] does not trip in that cycle because it reads
the override as of the last cycle. `Scenario_Override_Ends_By_Radio` is in
`EVC_Test_Authority`: `EVC_Test_Procedures` has no radio harness. It fails
with the two inputs forced False. Rows 5.8.4.1 f) and g) are done.

### The fixed Train Data entry, second package: the driver's train type taken by the on-board, the type in force in the data view, the DMI's hello (e6/fixed-entry-2) (2026-10-25)

- MSG_DRIVER_DATA kind 2: 14 bytes, the kind, the 12 bytes of the Train
  Data, then train_type u8 (0 the items entered one by one, 1 .. the
  count of MSG_TRAIN_TYPES the type chosen on the fixed layout).
  Decision: the 13-byte form stays readable as type 0
  (`Driver_Data_Train_Short_Length`), like the short form of
  MSG_STORED_VALUES: `Sim_Onboard_Env` (the bench page's scripted
  driver, not this package's) and a dozen on-board scenarios send it;
  no golden moved by the length. The DMI sends the index
  (`DMI_Train_Data.Stored_Type_Index`; the fixed entry's axle load,
  airtight and gauge now the type's own codes, like its categories).
  Premise of the brief corrected: the kind 2 bytes are decoded by
  `EVC_Driver_Requests.Take_Data` (`Train_Entry_T.Type_Index`), not by
  `EVC_Core.Inputs`; the data are taken in `EVC_Mission.Take_Data`.
  Decision: `EVC_Mission.Type_Matches` refuses an index above
  `EVC_Config.Default_Train_Type_Count` or items that differ from the
  type's (DMI 11.3.9.6 a: the driver cannot change a value of the
  type), by the path of every invalid entry (`Event_Refused` 2, the
  Train Data unchanged). `EVC_Train_Data.Set` gains `T : Type_Index_T
  := 0`, `Type_In_Force` (0 after `Clear`, `Start_Manoeuvre_Set`; kept
  by `Invalidate` with the data). `@req 3.18.3.2` on both; matrix row
  3.18.3.2 extended.
- MSG_STORED_VALUES: 65 bytes, train_type u8 at the end (0 none);
  `EVC_DMI_Port.Stored_Train_T.Type_Index`, filled by
  `EVC_Core.Outputs.Send_Stored_Values` from `Type_In_Force` (a change
  of the type alone resends the frame). The 64-byte form is no longer
  read (the protocol's rule; no sender of it). The DMI:
  `DMI_Train_Data.Take_Onboard (..., Type_Index)`, `Onboard_Type_Text`;
  `DMI_Data_View` follows Table 44 for the fixed entry (11.5.1.4): item
  3 'Train type' inserted, the rows numbered as the items of Tables 44
  and 45; decision (`Type_Row`): item 3 is shown while the Train data
  window offers its fixed layout or the stored data are a type's (the
  on-board's once its long form came, else the DMI's own entry).
- MSG_DMI_HELLO 16#43#, no payload (B2080): queued by
  `DMI_Core.Initialise`, the DMI's first frame; `EVC_Core.Handle_Input`
  at the DMI port (the parent, where the DMI frames are latched; the
  brief named `EVC_Core.Inputs`) resets `Types_Sent`, `Stored_Sent`,
  `Version_Sent` and `Contact_Sent`, so the next cycle sends
  MSG_TRAIN_TYPES, MSG_STORED_VALUES, MSG_SYSTEM_VERSION and a stored
  RBC contact again. The other change-driven messages are B2120.
  `EVC_DMI_Port.Valid_Input_Frame` accepts it, `Is_DMI_Hello`.
- Scenarios: `EVC_Test_Train_Data.Scenario_Train_Type` (type 2 in
  force and in MSG_STORED_VALUES, the short form type 0, index 3 and
  the passenger data named type 1 refused, type 1); `DMI_Test_Data_Entry`
  (the index on the wire, 0 flexible and 2 fixed; the data view of the
  fixed entry, golden `data_view_fixed`; the on-board's type 1 named
  Locomotive, a 64-byte MSG_STORED_VALUES ignored; the hello the first
  frame); `EVC_Test_Core.Scenario_End_To_End` (the hello before the
  first cycle; part 3, the DMI restarted, the types and the stored
  values reach it again); fourteen on-board goldens re-recorded
  (MSG_STORED_VALUES a byte longer). Fuzzers: `evc_fuzz` the long kind
  2 form with indices 0 .. 3 (from the drawn length, its random stream

### Review of the fifty-second round: ten verdicts re-derived blind (e5/review-52) (2026-10-25)

Each verdict below was written from the trace, the data and the clause
before the author's record was read; the code on master is the
author's record where no triage or backlog line was named.

1. 3131040_17 SV30 step 57. Mine: the runner's bench model. The
   workbook places the SBI 411.91 m and the EBI 234.79 m before the EOA
   at 85.5 km/h, the steps 54 and 57 say 412 m and 235 m, so the
   sequence's train keeps 85.5 km/h under the service brake from
   1088 m to 1265 m; our bench braked under our service brake and never
   reached the EBI. The on-board was right. The rule `EB_After_SB`
   (bench SB off when an expected EB at a later location follows an
   expected SB with no input between) catches 3131040_17, _53 and _54
   in sv30, the last two already marked "SB must be disabled". Author
   (S8e8f4487, model; B2040): the same. Agree. Remark: step 57 passes
   with ours at 68 km/h at 1265 m with the EB latched, so our EB came
   tens of metres before 1265 m; the runner does not place an EB step,
   whether ours is early is not traced (B2205).
2. 3130237_01 SV30 step 74. Mine: BG1d links BG3 at 340 m (890 m,
   Q_LOCACC 10 m); the window of the optional step 58 (not met) drove
   the train past 890 m and BG3d was read after its expectation window,
   its message rejected (3.4.4.4.3.2): its MA of 1500 m and packet 5
   not in force, our EOA stayed at about 1536 m, hence the SB at
   1399 m and the trip. Runner's fault; ending an expectation's wait at
   the next input's group (`Next_Group_Reached`) is the right reading

   further on in sv30). Author (S256875a4, model; B2041,
   `EVC_Position.Check_Window` Late): the same. Agree. Remark: B2041

   settle (B2201).
3. 3131040_17 step 62 (SV21, SV22, SV30). Mine: EOA = BG2d 500 m +
   L_ENDSECTION 1000 m = 1500 m; the step's 1455 m is 45 m in rear of
   it, where the min safe antenna cannot have passed the EOA (4.6.3
   [12]); Q_NVEMRRLS is the default (only at standstill, A.3.2), our
   EB was revoked at standstill and the runner then drove on at

### The hello's reach, the protocol's reasons, the position report in Reversing (e6/hello-reversing) (2026-10-25)

**The hello's reach (B2204, B2120 done).** The DMI messages sent only
once or at a change, sender by sender, with the decision for a restarted
DMI: MSG_TRAIN_TYPES (`Send_Train_Types`), MSG_STORED_VALUES
(`Send_Stored_Values`), MSG_SYSTEM_VERSION (`Send_System_Version`),
MSG_RBC_CONTACT (`Send_RBC_Contact`, when a contact is stored): resent
already (their markers reset by the hello); MSG_STATUS (`Send_Status`:
every cycle while the position is known, else at a change of brake, TTI,
radio, reversing, slippery rail, BMM, SM direction or tunnel): resent,
the hello sets `Geo_Sent`, so the next cycle sends it once with the
position or "unknown" whatever the `Status_*_Sent` markers hold;
MSG_TRACK_COND (sent by `EVC_Core.Stored.Evaluate_Stored_Information`,
not by Outputs) and MSG_VBC_LIST (`Send_VBC_List`): resent, the lists as
they are, empty included, through a new `EVC_Core.DMI_Restarted` set by
the hello, read by both and cleared by `Send_VBC_List` (its post).
Not resent: MSG_MODE_LEVEL, MSG_ONBOARD, MSG_SPEED_STATE (every cycle),
MSG_RADIO_NETWORKS (on the driver's request), the TIU outputs (`TIU_Sent`,
`TIU_Reasons_Sent`, `TIU_RS_Sent`, `TC_Sent`: the TIU port; premise of

(`EB_After_SB`); the lab's kept 85.5 km/h over the 177 m from the SBI

### The FRMCS registration event and the driver informed of the safe consist length unavailable (e6/protocol-decisions) (2026-10-26)

**The FRMCS registration (B1641).** 3.5.6.1.3: "As soon as it is
powered-up, the FRMCS on-board equipment reports continuously to the
ETCS on-board equipment whether it is registered or not to the FRMCS
radio network". The RTM port carries it as two events of the 3 byte
frame, 7 registered and 8 not registered (`EVC_Ports.RTM_Event_T`
`FRMCS_Registered`, `FRMCS_Not_Registered`, the format at the end of
`EVC_Ports`); the session byte must be 1 or 2 like every event and is
not read, the FRMCS on-board being one for the train (3.5.6.1.2). The
first report since the power-up of the ETCS on-board is the FRMCS
on-board "detected to be connected", the start of the 40 s of A.3.1
(page 218, "Time from when the FRMCS on-board equipment has been
detected to be connected ... registration is considered as failed").
`EVC_Sessions.Take_Event` passes both to `EVC_Sessions.Network.Take_FRMCS`
before the session check; `FRMCS_Registered` is the latest report with
FRMCS installed (decision 2 of e5/registration replaced). The wait of
5.4.3.2 S4 (`EVC_Sessions.Network.Supervise_Wait`): FRMCS the only
system for the stored type (FRMCS, or FRMCS+GSM-R with FRMCS alone
installed) ends at the registration (E61) or 40 s after the detection
(E71); both systems end when both are registered (E62; either once the
driver elected one radio system) or 40 s after the latest GSM-R order
(E72); the GSM-R case unchanged (E6 / E7). A42 shows entry 33 "FRMCS
network registration failed" for FRMCS and entry 34 for GSM-R, each
for the system not registered (`Evaluate`'s new `FRMCS_Failed`,
`EVC_Sessions.Apply_Network`). The SUBSET-076 bench reports event 8 in
the first cycle after each power-up where FRMCS is installed and never
event 7: the sequences' laboratory had no FRMCS simulator ("for the
time being, without FRMCS simulator available in laboratory", the
comments of feature 5040300), and their timer steps of A.3.1 say

### Three decisions: the VBC validity clock, the VBC capacity, the local time (e6/protocol-decisions) (2026-10-26)

Three papers for the user, no code. Each gives the clauses as printed,
what the code does, the options with the units they touch and their
effect on the proofs and the image formats, and one recommendation.

**1. The clock of a VBC's validity period (B1060).** 3.15.9.1 b): a
VBC is defined by its marker and country "b) Its validity period";
3.15.9.5: retained over No Power and "shall remain applicable when
powered on again. It shall be deleted when: a) it is ordered by
trackside, or b) its validity period has elapsed, or c) it is removed
by the driver (during Start of Mission), or d) a mismatch ..."; 3.15.9.6:
"The validity period shall start at the time the balise group message
is received or shall start at the time the VBC is entered by the
driver." T_VBC is 8 bits of 24 hours, up to 255 days
(7.5.1.154.1). The code: `EVC_VBC.Cover_T`
holds `Left`, the period left in ms; `EVC_VBC.Expire (Now_Ms)` takes the
time since its last call off every cover; `EVC_VBC.Keep` / `Restore`
carry the covers over No Power in `EVC_Retained.Kept_T.VBC` (a memory
of the host, no byte image yet), so the time without power is not
counted. `EVC_Core.Set_UTC` gives the UTC at the on-board time 0
(seconds since 2000), used today by the juridical records only.
Options: (a) as now: a cover outlives its calendar end by every hour
the train stood without power, a cover of one day set before a
weekend's stabling is applied on Monday; no cost. (b) the end in UTC:
`Cover_T` gains the end (UTC seconds, `Unsigned_32`: 255 days of T_VBC
are 22 million s, no overflow before 2135) when UTC is known at the
set, `Expire` deletes a cover whose end is past once UTC is known,
the time left kept as now for a cover set without UTC and as the
judgement while UTC is unknown after a power-up; units `EVC_VBC`
(Set, Expire, Cover_T, the proof of two comparisons), `EVC_Core` (the
UTC passed to Set and Expire), `EVC_Retained` unchanged in shape (the
record grows by 16 x 5 bytes in memory); a scenario over a power cycle;
no image format (EVC_Retained has none). (c) a real-time clock of the
target (E8): it is what (b) reads through `Set_UTC`, not a separate
design. Recommendation: (b). "Its validity period has elapsed" is
calendar time: a period of days given by trackside for a work site
does not stop when the train is switched off; the UTC already reaches
the core, and the fallback keeps today's behaviour where it is
unknown.

**2. The capacity of the VBC store (B1063).** The clauses printed
(3.15.9.1 to 3.15.9.6) state no number of covers and no source
priority. The code: one store of `EVC_VBC.VBC_Max` (16, the DMI's
list length `DMI_Protocol.VBC_List_Max`) for the driver's and
trackside's covers; a new identity when it is full is ignored, the
DMI's Set VBC disabled (national bit 2, `EVC_VBC.Full`); the same
identity replaces its cover (3.15.9.4) whatever the fill. Options: (a)
as now; (b) separate rooms, 16 for the driver's covers (the DMI list)
and N for trackside's: `EVC_VBC` (a source per cover, two counts), the
DMI list of the driver's only or of both (the protocol's list length
fixed at 16: a protocol change if both are listed), `EVC_Retained`
grows; the limit moves, it does not go away; (c) a trackside order
when full replaces the oldest cover: `EVC_VBC.Set` (the cover with the
least time left); no format change. Recommendation: (a). 3.15.9.5's
list of deletions is closed ("It shall be deleted when: a) ... d)"):
(c) deletes a cover for none of its four reasons, and (b) only moves
the limit; a store limit is a capacity of the implementation, and 16
covers at once is beyond the use the clauses describe (works and
commissioning areas). What stays to do with (a): the store's capacity
named in the installation documentation, the ignored trackside order
recorded (a backlog item if the user wants it).

**3. The local time (B1340).** 3.18.5.1: "Each ERTMS/ETCS on-board
equipment shall be able to provide the date (day, month, year) and
time (hour, minute, second) in Universal Time Co-ordinated (UTC) and
Local Time."; 3.18.5.2: "The local time shall be presented to the
driver, while the UTC shall be used for the juridical data."; SUBSET-027
4.2.3.3 DATE (YEAR 7 bits, 127 "year unknown"; MONTH, DAY) and 4.2.3.4
"TIME ... in Universal Time Co-ordinated (UTC)" (HOUR, MINUTES, SECONDS,
TTS). The code: `EVC_Core.Set_UTC` (the port's UTC at time 0) feeds
the juridical DATE and TIME (`EVC_Outbox.Build_JRU`, "unknown" without
it); the driver is shown the on-board clock since time 0 (the seconds
of MSG_STATUS and of the text messages). Options: (a) an installation
value of `EVC_Config`, the offset of the local time to UTC in signed
minutes: the image's format version 3 (a field of 2 bytes, the decoder
and encoder, the proof of the image's validity, the bench's and the
runner's images), and the summer time either a second value with no
rule to switch it or wrong half of the year; (b) the offset given by
the port with the UTC (`Set_UTC` extended, or a `Set_Local_Offset`
beside it): the clock source of the host (the train's clock, a GNSS
receiver, the target's real-time clock) knows the time zone and its
summer time, the core adds the offset to `UTC_Seconds + Clock_Ms /
1000` for MSG_STATUS and the text messages once both are known and
keeps the clock since time 0 otherwise; units `EVC_Core` (the entry and
two fields), `EVC_Core.Outputs` (the seconds sent), the hosts that call
`Set_UTC` (`Sim_Onboard_Env`, `S076_Bench`, ports/hosted); no image
format, nothing to prove beyond the range of the sum; (c) as now, not
3.18.5.1 / 3.18.5.2. Recommendation: (b). The local time depends on
the date and the region (the summer time twice a year, a train crossing
a time zone border), which an installation constant cannot follow and
the core has no clause to compute; the port that already gives the UTC
is the one that knows it.

The three backlog lines stay open with this paper's reference: the user
decides.

### Review of the fifty-fourth round: eight verdicts re-derived blind (e5/review-54) (2026-10-26)

Each verdict below was written from the clause, the data and the trace
before the author's record was read. All eight items were taken.

1. Table 4.8.4 footnote [1] (PDF page 76). Mine: in PT a message needs
   level 2 and the Recognition of Exit from TR with a more recent time
   stamp; level 1 rejects; PT is used in levels 1 and 2 only
   (4.4.14.2.1), so a context whose level is not valid satisfies neither
   branch and is rejected (the case does not arise in PT). `EVC_Radio_
   Acceptance.In_PT` (Trip_Exit_Known, a valid level 2) matches; the
   builders of the radio `Context_T` (`EVC_Radio_Authority` from
   `EVC_Levels`, `EVC_Sessions.Network.Accepts` and `Take_Radio_Order`
   from the parameters that `EVC_Sessions` fills with `EVC_Levels.Valid`
   and `EVC_Levels.Level`) all pass the level. Author (e6/acceptance-
   level): the same, `Take_Radio_Order` was the one that left the level
   out and now takes it. Agree.
2. The override before S10. Mine: 5.4.5.3 a) allows it at S10 and S20
   only, with 5.8.2.1 for SB (level 2, validated Train Data and train
   running number); 4.10 gives TBR for both on entering SB, so a first
   S10 (before S12) refuses by c), an S10 reached again after S12 (D11
   without a session, A32, A40, D8 / D9, E15) and S20 allow. DMI Table 34
   #1 does not know the S-state and enables the button in SB with the
   data valid, also at S11 and S21 to S25: the on-board refuses there.
   `EVC_Procedures.Override_Allowed` refuses S21 to S25 (`SoM_Started`)
   and S11 (`TD_Ack_Awaited`). Author: the same, the S11 defect fixed,
   the DMI's enabling a decision (B2320). Agree; one point undecided: the
   author's "refused at S1 to S4 by 5.8.2.1 c)" holds on the first pass;
   a return from S20 by 5.4.5.3 e) or j) (the level or the Radio data
   re-entered, S2 / S3, then S4 and A31) keeps the Train Data validated at
   S12 (no new entry into SB), and nothing in `Override_Allowed` refuses
   S4 or A31 then (S2, S3 and S12 are entry windows, no button
   reachable): B2402.
3. The FRMCS registration at S4. Mine: FRMCS alone ends at E61 (A31) or
   40 s (A.3.1) after the FRMCS on-board was detected as connected (E71,
   A42); both systems end at E62 or 40 s after the latest GSM-R order
   (E72), the FRMCS detection does not time that case; for a port that
   reports only registered / not registered the first report after the
   power-up is the detection, and an S4 reached later than 40 s after it
   fails at once. `EVC_Sessions.Network.Take_FRMCS` and `Supervise_Wait`
   and the bench (event 8 in the first cycle after each power-up, never
   registered) do exactly that. Agree. A remark, no line: a port that
   never reports leaves the FRMCS-alone wait without an end (no
   detection, no E71); literal, the port's contract has to report at
   connection.
4. Three decisions. (a) The VBC validity: mine, the end in UTC judged
   when UTC is known, the powered clock as a lower bound that may end it
   too; the author's (b), the same. Agree. (b) The capacity: mine,
   separate rooms of at least 20 for the driver's covers and at least 10
   for trackside's, from SUBSET-040 4.5.1.2 ("at least 20 VBCs set by the
   driver") and 4.3.2.1 w) (10 memorised from trackside, its remark: not
   including the driver's 20); the author's (a), one store of 16, since
   SUBSET-026 3.15.9 names no number. Disagree: the paper did not read
   SUBSET-040, whose minima a shared 16 does not meet; DMI 11.2.4.5.1 #5
   (Set VBC enabled while "the maximum on-board storage capacity of VBC
   set by driver is not reached, see [4] 4.5.1.2") counts the driver's
   covers apart: B2400. (c) The local time: mine and the author's, the
   offset from the port that gives the UTC. Agree.
5. A.3.5.1 4th and 7th bullets. Mine: after a roll-back behind a mode
   profile's end and forward again FS does not come a second time; the OS
   acknowledgement is shown in the rectangle (5.9.3.2) and again at the
   entry when not given (5.9.3.7), never again after a roll-back; behind a
   track condition's start (5.18.2.3) the announcement is not shown again.
   `EVC_Procedures.Note_Passed` latches the beginning and the end per slot;
   `Scenario_Mode_Profile_Roll_Back` expects exactly that;
   `Scenario_Track_Condition_Roll_Back` expects it too but is not called,

### The track conditions over a reverse movement fixed, the MA timers and the TAF request over a reverse movement (e6/roll-back-2) (2026-10-27)

**B2341, A.3.5.1 7th bullet, the track conditions over a reverse
movement** (fixed). The claim held at the source: `EVC_Track_Conditions.
Evaluate` and `External` judged every phase against the train's position
in each cycle, and the records 45 took their phase from the signs of the
distances of the train interface's items (`EVC_JRU_Records.
Track_Conditions`, `To_Start > 0`, `To_End < 0`), so a roll back behind
a location wrote them again. `EVC_Track_Conditions.Phases` judges the
locations of an element (point C and the start by the max safe front
end, the end by the min safe front end, the start and the end by the
min safe rear end; the sound horn and the radio hole by the estimated
front end against the estimated items; a change of traction system or
of allowed current a single location), each one ORed with its flag in
`EVC_Profiles.Stored_T` (`Announced`, `Started`, `Ended`,
`Rear_Started`; the end by the rear is the existing `Noted`); `Evaluate`
keeps them first (its nested `Keep`) for the four stores (the
conditions, the traction and current changes, the platforms), then
shows from the flags; `External` reads `Phases` (the same answer
whatever the order of the two in the cycle) and gives each item its
`Phase` (0 the start not reached, 1 reached, 2 the end passed by the
min safe front end), which the record 45 takes. Decision: the
remaining distances of 5.20.2.3 (not in the bullet's list) follow the
train; only their start and stop (5.20.2.2, .4, .5) are kept. Kind 0
(the non stopping areas: the virtual limits of the supervision) and the
big metal masses (`BMM_At_Antenna`) are unchanged, as A.3.5.1.1 says.
The scenario's expectations (the lowered pantograph kept and the
announcement not shown again behind the start, 5.18.2.3; the raise
pantograph kept behind the end, 5.18.2.5; the distance to the start not
generated again behind the rear end's location, 5.20.2.4; no record 45
again) are the clauses'; `Scenario_Track_Condition_Roll_Back` is called
from `evc_test.adb`. Size: `Evaluate` and `External` stay within their
known lines (the kind of the external item to `External_Kind`). Proof of
`evc_track_conditions` (247 checks), `evc_jru_records` (445) and
`evc_profiles` (590), none unproved; runner 0 regressions, 0
improvements (no sequence moved). Edits outside the brief's units:
`EVC_Profiles.Stored_T` (the four flags), `EVC_JRU_Records.
Track_Conditions` (the phase of the item), `EVC_Test_JRU.
Scenario_JRU_Track_Conditions` (the new component in its aggregates).
Left of the 7th bullet: the relocation (B781).

**A.3.5.1 12th bullet, the MA timers over a reverse movement** (no
defect). Wrong premise of the brief: the timers live in
`EVC_Movement_Authority` (`Supervise`, the `End_Timer` and `OL_Timer` of
the MA), not in `EVC_Radio_Authority`, and their scenarios in

### The events shown again after a DMI restart, the override from S20 back, the safe consist text (e6/dmi-restart) (2026-10-27)

**The events after a DMI restart (B2240 done).** The claim held at
the source: `EVC_Core.Outputs.Send_Procedure_Messages` sent
MSG_SYSTEM_STATUS and MSG_TEXT / MSG_TEXT_REMOVE as the events of the
cycle only. The texts: `EVC_Text_Messages` keeps every message in a
slot with `Shown` (set at the display, the slot cleared at the
removal) and `Acked`; a text whose end came before its acknowledgement
keeps its slot, its brake and `Shown` until the acknowledgement (the
brake was kept without the text being shown on a restarted DMI: the
open question of the line, answered by reading `Evaluate`). The system
status messages: the owners know only their events
(`EVC_Procedures.Status_Event`, `EVC_Sessions.Status_Event`,
`EVC_Radio_Authority.Status_Entry`, and the `*_Shown` markers of
`Show_Mode_Indications`, `Show_Route_Unsuitable`,
`Show_Trackside_Malfunction`), six senders, and none of them knows the
ends the DMI owns alone (its 30 s timers, its mode changes of 15.1.1.2,
the acknowledgements) which `EVC_JRU_Records.System_Status` takes from
MSG_STATUS_ENDED and the driver's acknowledgements. Decision: the JRU's
set is the list to resend, being the set "displayed as the on-board
sees it"; kept by entry beside its SUBSET-027 bits (`Entries_Shown`,
`Entry_Shown`), because a bit is shared by two entries (1 and 2, 4 and
5, 15 and 16, 17 and 18: the brake and the trip rows) — the smaller
change than an accessor in six owners that would still miss the DMI's
own ends. In the cycle after the hello `Send_Procedure_Messages`
(before `Send_VBC_List`, which clears `DMI_Restarted`, the order in
the spec) sends `Resend_Texts` (every slot shown, the hour and minute
of its first display, the acknowledgement bit only while awaited) in
place of the cycle's text starts (a start of the cycle is in a shown
slot already), the cycle's removals as they are, then
`Resend_Status_Entries`: a start for every entry the set held at the
end of the last cycle and that no status event of this cycle names
(`EVC_Outbox.Status_Event`: a start sent already, or an end). The DMI
does not show a duplicate (read in `DMI_Text_Messages.Put`: the same
id replaces its slot; `DMI_System_Status.Start`: an active entry
begins its end conditions anew, no second text). An entry ended by the
DMI's own timer while no DMI was connected is shown again, its timer
restarting: what the on-board saw. The comment of MSG_DMI_HELLO in
common/dmi_protocol.ads says both. Scenario
`EVC_Test_Procedures.Scenario_DMI_Restart_Displayed` (FS, level 1):
three plain texts, one acknowledged before the restart (removed), one
not acknowledged after its 3 s (Q_TEXTCONFIRM 2, the service brake),
"Train data changed" with its brake while moving (5.17.2.2 S2); after
the hello the two texts displayed shown again (flags 4 and 5: the
second with the request), not the acknowledged one, the starts of
entries 18 and 6 ("Entering FS" of the mode set at the start: its end
is the DMI's, no DMI reports it in the generic), nothing in the next
cycle, and the acknowledgement on the restarted DMI releases the text's
brake. Proofs `evc_core-outputs`, `evc_text_messages`,
`evc_jru_records`. Runner 1163 / 1069 / 958, 0 movements.

**The override from S20 back (B2402 done).** 5.4.5.3 a): "only at S10
and S20". The claim held: from S20, j) (level 2: S3, then A31 or S4)
and e) (S2, D3, S3 ...) leave the Train Data validated at S12 and the
train running number valid (no entry into SB, so 4.10's TBR does not
apply), and neither `SoM_Started` (`EVC_Mission.Waiting_For_RBC`,
`Proposed`) nor `TD_Ack_Awaited` holds there. `EVC_Mission` has no
step of the start of mission; `EVC_Sessions.Mission` has one
(`Step_T`: Opening from A31 until D31, Decided with `Awaiting_Network`
for S4 after D7) and exposes it (`EVC_Sessions.SoM_Opening`,
`SoM_Awaiting_Registration`). Fix: `EVC_Procedures.Context_T.SoM_Opening`
(both, built in `EVC_Core.Modes.Run_Procedures`), and
`Override_Allowed` refuses the override in SB while it holds; S2 and
S3 are the DMI's entry windows, which the on-board does not see until
the entry. Scenario `EVC_Test_Sessions.Scenario_SoM_L2_Override_From_S20`
(two sessions configured): the start of mission to S20 as in
`Scenario_SoM_L2_Override_Before_S10`, the Radio data re-entered with
RBC 301, the session being established (A31): the override taken
before the fix (run with the refusal removed), refused now; the
session opened, S10: taken. With one session configured the opening
was judged failed in the next cycle (A32, S10: the override then
allowed by a) at S10), the session to RBC 300 neither terminated nor
the one to RBC 301 attempted: B2420, not traced. The DMI's EOA button
(`DMI_Conditions.Override_EOA`, DMI Table 34 #1) is enabled at A31 and
S4 as at S11 (read, not run): B2320 covers it. Row 5.4.5.3 a) noted.
Proofs `evc_procedures`, `evc_core-modes` (the parent unchanged).

**The safe consist length unavailable (B1401, the paper; its premise
wrong).** 4.4.21.1.12: "If the safe consist length information is
acquired from an external source and it becomes unavailable, the
ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall inform the driver and the trackside
and, if the train is not at standstill, it shall command the service
brake." The line's premise (no system status message for it in the
DMI of 4.0.0) is wrong at the source: Table 68 of the DMI
specification (15.1.1.5, PDF page 314) has "Safe consist length no
longer available", start condition 4.4.21.1.12, end "Message displayed
for 30 s (if 3.14.1.7.6 fulfilled beforehand or if brake command
reason revoked as per 4.12.1.2 beforehand), 3.14.1.7.6 (if message
displayed for 30 s beforehand), Brake command reason revoked as per
4.12.1.2 (if message displayed for 30 s beforehand)", row "Brake
reason". Our DMI has it already: `SS_Safe_Consist_Length` = 19 in
common/dmi_protocol.ads, `DMI_System_Status`'s catalogue row
(`T_Safe_Consist`, `After_30s`, the brake modes), and SUBSET-027's
SYSTEM_STATUS_MESSAGE has its bit 31 (`EVC_JRU_Records.SS_Bit`'s
comment: "has no entry of the on-board"). What is missing is on the
on-board alone: `EVC_DMI_Port` has no entry 19 (its SS_* go from 18 to
20), no unit sends it, and `SS_Bit` maps nothing to bit 31. The three
ways of the brief: (1) a new system status entry with its text,
numbered after the table's last: not needed, the table has the row;
(2) a plain text of 3.12.3 generated on board: against 15.1.1.1 (the
system status messages "shall be displayed ... as specified in Table
68") and it would bypass the row's end conditions; (3) nothing beyond
the brake and the button: leaves 4.4.21.1.12 "inform the driver"
unfulfilled where the specification provides the means.
Recommendation, no decision of the user needed: the entry of Table 68,
with no change of dmi/ or of the protocol. The on-board's part, a build
item: `EVC_DMI_Port.SS_Safe_Consist_Length` (19); the loss as an event
of the cycle (today `Lost` is local to
`EVC_Stored_Information.Consist_Shortening`, SM or SB with the
manoeuvre set, standstill or not; an accessor beside `Consist_Brake`),
the start of entry 19 at the loss in the owner of the brake's reasons
(`EVC_Procedures`, beside `Consist_SB`, the shape of entry 1 at
`Link_SB`), its end left to the DMI (the 30 s, the acknowledgement of
3.14.1.7.6, the reason revoked: the DMI's row) or sent at the release
of `Consist_SB` (4.12.1.2); `SS_Bit (19)` = 31; a scenario where the
input of TIU signal 15 goes unavailable in SM while moving (the
service brake and entry 19) and at standstill (entry 19, no brake).
Left: the package's bound came after the paper (B1401 narrowed to
that build item).

   5.20.2.2, .4, .5, not 5.20.2.3; the announcement at C, "Lowered
   pantograph" at D, "Raise pantograph" at E and its timer, the start of

   Conditions.Phases` latches Announced / Started / Ended / Rear_Started
   in `EVC_Profiles.Stored_T`, the output computes D - max front and E -
   min front every cycle, `Has_Start` from the latch. Author
   (e6/roll-back-2): the same decision. Agree; a remark, no line: the
   scenario does not check that the distance to E follows the train back.
2. A.3.5.1 9th bullet. Mine: shown from 3.15.5.2 a) to b) or the
   acknowledgement; the start and the stop are both kept, so a roll-back
   behind the beginning keeps it shown, one behind the end does not show
   it again; a new packet 34 replaces the stored request (3.15.5.6), also
   one shown, and its own start is taken afresh. `Evaluate_TAF` latches
   `Begun`, `Stored` is cleared at the end, `Take_TAF` rebuilds the record.
   Author: the defect (withdrawn and shown twice) found by the scenario
   and fixed so. Agree; no scenario of a second packet 34 over a shown
   request (a remark).
3. The override from S20 back, and the RBC changed. Mine: (a) a) allows
   it at S10 and S20 only; S2 / S3 (entry windows), S4, A31, D31 and A32
   do not, S10 after A32 does; `Override_Allowed` refusing `SoM_Opening`
   (Opening or the registration awaited) matches. (b) 3.5.3.5.2 decides
   the second question whatever the number of sessions configured: "the
   existing communication session(s) shall be terminated ... and the new
   one shall be established" (3.5.3.5.2.1 excepts the Accepting RBC of a
   handover only): terminate 300 and open 301, a refusal is not a reading.

   calls `Open`, which with no idle slot parks the request in `Pending`;

   being established, not that the session to 300 is terminated.

### The VBC store built to SUBSET-040: 20 covers set by the driver and 10 from trackside, the DMI's list of 30 (e6/vbc-capacity) (2026-10-27)

B1063 built as the user decided it (B2400): the premises checked at the
source first. SUBSET-040 4.5.1.2: "The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment
shall be able to store at least 20 VBCs set by the driver" (reference
SUBSET-026 3.15.9.2; justification: a cross-border cold movement); 4.3.2.1
w): at most 10 packets 6 in one message, 10 memorised on-board, the
remark "does not include the minimum number of VBCs set by driver" (rule
4.5.1.2). SUBSET-026 3.15.9.5's deletions are a closed list (a) ordered
by trackside, b) the period elapsed, c) removed by the driver, d) a
country mismatch); 3.15.9.4: a VBC of a stored identity replaces the
stored one with its period. DMI 11.2.4.5.1: Set VBC enabled while "the
maximum on-board storage capacity of VBC set by driver is not reached,
see [4] 4.5.1.2", Remove VBC while at least one is stored. DMI 11.3.13.4:
the Remove VBC window is the entry of a code in one field, not a list;
the list of covers stored is shown by the Data view (Table 45, "VBC #n
set code", windows "2..n"). The code before: one store of 16
(`EVC_VBC.VBC_Max`, the driver's and trackside's alike, a new identity
ignored when full), `EVC_VBC.Set` called by both
`EVC_Core.Inputs.Take_VBC_Requests` and
`EVC_Stored_Information.Take_VBC_Orders`, the DMI's list of 16
(`DMI_Protocol.VBC_List_Max`, and its copy `EVC_DMI_Port.VBC_List_Max`).

1. The store (`EVC_VBC`): `Driver_Max` 20 and `Trackside_Max` 10 named
   with their rules (`@req 3.15.9.2` and `@req 7.4.2.2.1`, the clauses
   SUBSET-040 cites), `VBC_Max` their sum 30, an `Origin_T` (Driver,
   Trackside) on each cover; `Set` is the driver's, `Order` packet 6's
   (`EVC_Stored_Information.Take_VBC_Orders` calls it: a one-line edit
   outside the units); a new identity is taken while the room of its
   origin is not full, else ignored: no cover is deleted for it, since
   none of the four deletions of 3.15.9.5 applies. `Full` (MSG_ONBOARD's
   national bit 2, the DMI's Set VBC) counts the driver's covers alone,
   `Count` both (the list). Decision: a VBC of a stored identity replaces
   the stored one in the room it already takes, whoever gives it
   (3.15.9.4): a VBC is its identity and its period (3.15.9.1 a), b)),
   the room is the store's accounting, so the counts can never pass
   their rooms; the other reading (the replacing VBC takes its giver's
   room) would let trackside's count pass 10 when it replaces a driver's
   cover, and the driver's 20 would no longer be guaranteed. The retained
   layout: `EVC_Retained.Kept_T` keeps `EVC_VBC.Kept_T`, the 30 covers
   with their origin; the store is a memory within one run of the host
   (its header: no non-volatile image, no CRC yet), so no image of an
   older layout exists to reject or convert. Until the protocol's list
   grew, `EVC_Core.Outputs.Send_VBC_List` capped the list at
   `VBC_List_Max` (a `Natural'Min` that stays, a no-op at 30 against 30).

   untouched and Set VBC enabled; 21 driver's covers, 20 taken, the 21st

**B2601 with B2621, the Radio Network type at S3: built.** 5.4.3.2 S3

is installed on-board and the FRMCS on-board is not registered to the

"inform the driver that the FRMCS network registration has failed. The
process shall then go to D8"; D8: "If the stored Radio Network type is
FRMCS+GSM-R while both radio systems are installed on-board, the process
shall go back to S3. Otherwise, the process shall go to S10". The DMI's
Table 49 (ERA_ERTMS_015560 11.7.2.4, page 236) is the same: S3-4 E5 ->
A41 -> D10 -> S3-1 or S10. The reviewer's cause (B2621) held at the
source: `EVC_Sessions.Network.Driver_Entries` stored the type with no
branch for E4, and `Supervise_Wait` timed the FRMCS registration out
only In_SoM (S4) and, with both systems, watched the latest GSM-R order
only (once the mobile registered, no time ran for FRMCS). The path after
A41 is D8 -> S3 (the reviewer's), not S4 (B2601's). The reading
(decision): E4's "not registered" is the registration considered failed,
which A.3.1 defines as the time "from when the FRMCS on-board equipment
has been detected to be connected ... after which the registration is
considered as failed" (40 s, `Registration_Time_Ms`), since A41 tells the
driver that it "has failed"; until that time the on-board waits as at S4,
which is what 5040300_24 shows (step 97 ST05 "the onboard still awaits
the registration", step 99 the A.3.1 timer, steps 100 / 101 entry 33 and
JRU 23 bit 24, step 102 the Radio data window "the process shall go back
to S3"). From the driver's seat: no failure is announced while the
registration may still succeed. Built: `Driver_Entries` sets `Type_Wait`
when the entered type is FRMCS or FRMCS+GSM-R, FRMCS installed (not
GSM-R only), FRMCS not registered, in SB (S3 is a step of the start of
mission); `Supervise_Wait` ends it at the FRMCS registration (no message,
the type stays stored, S3) or at 40 s from the FRMCS detection
(`FRMCS_At`), A41: `FRMCS_Failed` (entry 33); when the time is already
over at the entry, A41 in the same cycle; D8 is the wait's end (S3's
entries are taken again; S10 is the DMI's D10). A mode other than SB ends
it. The hour glass: `EVC_Sessions.SoM_Awaiting_Registration` is
`Mission.Awaiting_Registration or else Network.Type_Awaited` (MSG_ONBOARD
waiting 1 through the existing condition of `EVC_Core.Outputs`, the Main

### The runner's speed at a plateau of the chart, a comment read to its end, the one-radio-system step (e5/runner-speed) (2026-10-27)

**B2600, the speed at a plateau of the chart: built.** 3130700_03 SV30
traced on master: step 62 Overspeed (JRU 21 status 2, V_PERM 65) at 283
m, the train at 1806 cm/s. The chart's calibration is right: the
speedprofile's 65.4 km/h at 200 m is `Calibrated` 65.01 km/h (zero 0.2,
scale 0.997; the "mrsp" plateaus fit their multiples of 5 within 0.06
km/h); the cause is the conversion: `Kmh_To_Cms` rounds 65.01 km/h to
1806 cm/s, while the on-board takes a speed of the language as the floor
of K x 1250 / 9 (`EVC_Profiles` for V_STATIC, `EVC_PBD.Restrict` for
V_PBD): 65 km/h is 1805 cm/s, and 3.13.10.3.3 t2 (V_est > V_MRSP) gives
Overspeed for 1806. The corpus (SV30, a scratch print at the end of
every step): 1224 steps of 107 sequences end with the chart within 0.5
km/h of our permitted speed; at 368 steps of 36 sequences the train is
above it in cm/s (the rounding, or a drawing 0.1 km/h over); 7 sequences
fail first at such a step, 2 by the speed (3130700_03 step 62;
3130700_06 step 92, the chart's 10.1 km/h on V5 10, 281 cm/s against
277), the 5 others for causes that are not the speed (3070300_12 step 87
the level symbol, 4080454_01 step 125 a track condition, 5070300_04 step
75 the RTM's Q_DESK, 5160000_01 step 55 the LX symbol, 9990400_41 step
39 the mode). Decision in `S076_Run.Chart_Cms`: a chart speed within
0.5 km/h (the calibration's own band) of a multiple of 5 km/h is driven
at most at that multiple's cm/s as the on-board takes it, never raised
to it. A first try that snapped both ways raised 3131030_17's chart
(154.92 km/h at 1450 m, rising) to 4305 cm/s, above our V_warning 4304,
and failed its step 68 (3131030_17 to _19, the three versions): the cap
only lowers. The full runner 1169 / 1058 / 963 -> 1178 / 1051 / 961, 0
regressions: 3130700_03 and 3130700_06 (S8727c744) and 3131040_59
(S1fd323b5, its chart drawn at 102.5 for the ceiling 100) pass in the
three versions. Triage: S8727c744's model line and S1fd323b5 marked
fixed (S8727c744 stays at 3130700_04 step 65, its s076 line); B2600
done.

### The on-board tells the DMI whether the override is selectable; the desk scenario's terminating case; the consist heading (e6/override-bit) (2026-10-27)

B2320, the override selectable told to the DMI. The claim held at the
source: `DMI_Conditions.Override_EOA` was the DMI's own reading of DMI
Table 34 #1 (11.2.2.4: the speed limit of the override, the modes
FS/AD/LS/SR/OS/UN/SN/SH, SB with the Driver ID, the Train Data, the
train running number valid and level 2, PT with the Train Data and the
train running number), so it enabled the EOA button at S11 and at S21 to
S25 where `EVC_Procedures.Override_Allowed` refuses (`SoM_Started`,
`TD_Ack_Awaited`, `SoM_Opening`). The protocol's "override u8 (bool)" is
of MSG_MODE_LEVEL, the override active (5.8.3.7), not its selection.
Built: MSG_ONBOARD national bit 4 (the byte of the "allowed" bits, bits
4 to 7 were free; no length change), from
`EVC_Procedures.Override_Selectable`, a state of the override step set
each cycle to `Override_Allowed (C, NV)`, the answer a selection of that
cycle gets; `EVC_Core.Outputs.Send_Onboard` sets the bit; the constant
`EVC_DMI_Port.National_Override_Selectable`. Decisions: the bit carries
the speed term of 5.8.2.1 a) too (the driver sees the whole answer; train
bit 1 stays the speed term alone, the DMI no longer reads it), and
`Override_EOA` reads the bit alone: every term of the row names the
on-board's data, none is one the on-board cannot know, so the DMI keeps
none of its own (`DMI_Conditions.Override_Speed_OK` removed). Where the
two readings differed, the bit is the narrower (5.8.2.1 c) asks for the
data in every mode but SH, the row in SB only), except the Driver ID of
the row's SB branch, which `Override_Allowed` does not test; at S10 and
S20 it is valid (S1 before them). The DMI's own wrapper EVC
(`Test_Support`, a new `Override_Refused` input) and `EVC_Mock` set the
bit where Table 34 #1 read their data before, so no existing display
golden changed. Scenarios: `DMI_Test_Windows.Scenario_Override_Selectable`
(goldens `override_eoa_s11` disabled, `override_eoa_s10` enabled,
MSG_ONBOARD driven raw; at S21 `override_s21_main_waiting`, see below),
the Table 34 checks
of `Scenario_Enabling_Conditions` on the bit; `EVC_Test_Sessions`: the
bit clear at S1, S4, S11 (`Scenario_SoM_L2_Override_Before_S10`), A31
(`_From_S20`), S21, S24 (`Scenario_SoM_L2_SR_Proposal`), set at S20, S10
and in SR at standstill. Goldens: `evc/bench_onboard` (cycle group 7,
national 5 -> 21) and `evc/bench_level2` (hash only) re-recorded for the
bit. Rows 5.8.2.1, 5.8.2.1 c) noted; there is no matrix of the DMI
specification for 11.2.2.4 (the brief's "DMI row"). Proofs
`evc_procedures`, `evc_core-outputs`: no unproved check. Runner 1169 /
1058 / 963, 0 movements: the runner's override presses fall where the
on-board took them before.

The S21 check, corrected after the coordinator's blind description (the

### Review of the fifty-seventh round: eight verdicts re-derived blind (e5/review-57) (2026-10-27)

Each verdict below was written from the clause, the data and the trace
before the author's record (the four subsections above, the backlog,
the triage) was read. All eight items were taken.

1. The VBC store's rooms. Mine: SUBSET-040 4.5.1.2 (at least 20 set by
   the driver) and 4.3.2.1 w) (10 memorised, "not including" the
   driver's 20) are two rooms, 30 in all; a new identity when its
   origin's room is full is ignored, since 3.15.9.5's deletions are a
   closed list and no stored cover may make room for it; 3.15.9.4 names
   no room for a replacement from the other origin, and keeping the room
   it takes is the reading under which both minimums hold after any
   history and the "shall replace" never fails for want of room.
   `EVC_VBC.Put` matches the identity in either room first and keeps
   its origin, takes a new one only below its room; `Full` counts the
   driver's room; `vbc_rooms` covers the 11th order, the 21st set, an
   order with the driver's room full, the replacement in the driver's
   room and No Power. Author (e6/vbc-capacity): the same, the
   replacement in its room by decision with the same argument (the
   other reading lets trackside pass 10). Agree.
2. The Override EOA button. Mine: 5.4.5.3 a) allows the selection at
   S10 and S20 only, with 5.8.2.1 for SB (speed at most V_NVALLOWOVTRP,
   SB in level 2, validated Train Data and train running number). The
   driver reaches the Override window at S10, S11 and S20 (the Main
   window closable); at S21 the DMI is in Table 50 S7 (the Main window,
   every button and [close] disabled, 11.7.3.2), out of reach. Enabled
   at S10 and S20, not at S11, where every term of Table 34 #1's SB
   branch is true: the DMI cannot tell S11 from S20 and has no
   V_NVALLOWOVTRP, so the on-board decides. `Override_Allowed` excludes
   `SoM_Started`, `TD_Ack_Awaited` and `SoM_Opening`, MSG_ONBOARD
   national bit 4 carries it, `Override_EOA` reads the bit alone.
   Author (e6/override-bit): the same. Agree. Remark without a line: the
   scenario's second case and its golden `override_eoa_s10` are the
   state with the session open and the Train Data acknowledged, which is
   S20 (S10 is level 2 with no session, D11); the logic is right, the
   label is not.
3. The Radio network type at S3. Mine: S3's E4 is a condition at the
   entry and goes to A41 with no wait named; A41's "has failed" with
   A.3.1's FRMCS time (40 s from the FRMCS on-board's detection as
   connected) allows waiting within those 40 s (the hour glass) and A41
   at their end, at once when they are past, a registration in time
   ending the wait silently; after A41, D8: S3 with FRMCS+GSM-R and both
   systems installed, S10 otherwise. Author (e6/network-type): the same
   reading by decision, built in `Driver_Entries` (`Type_Wait`) and
   `Supervise_Wait`, with the scenario's five cases. Agree on the
   reading and the build, with a gap: the time counts from `FRMCS_At`,
   set only by `Take_FRMCS` at the FRMCS on-board's first report; an
   FRMCS installed that never reports leaves `Type_Wait` set for ever
   (the hour glass at S3, no A41), where E4 holds plainly and A.3.1's

   S3) and another bound: B2720.
4. The MA request parameters and Q_DIR. Mine: 4.9.1.3 deletes packet
   57's parameters on entering level 1 only, 4.10.1.3's row on entering
   NP; 3.6.3.1.3 takes from any medium only information valid for the
